newsitem.title: USA: Senate Superfund bill seeks to aid municipalities.
newsitem.headline: Senate Superfund bill seeks to aid municipalities.

text.p: The latest proposal by Republicans to overhaul the Superfund toxic waste clean-up program seeks to cap cost liability for local governments and offer them funds to redevelop abandoned industrial sites or "brownfield sites", Senate aides said Wednesday.

The bill, introduced Tuesday and released on Wednesday by Senate Environment and Public Works Chairman John Chafee, would authorize $15 million in annual grants to identify and characterize contamination at brownfield sites.
It would also authorize $25 million in annual grants to states and local governments to clean up brownfields.
Grants would be limited to $100,000 a year and $200,000 total for assessing contamination per site and would be limited to $150,000 annually and $300,000 total for cleaning up any one site.
It would also authorize $25 million in annual grants for States to improve voluntary clean-up programs.

Seeking to cut legal challenges on who should pay for cleaning up sites where many parties dumped waste, the bill would cap liability of municipal owners and operators of landfills at 10 percent of total costs if the community has fewer than 100,000 people. The cap would be set at 20 percent of clean-up costs for communities with a population greater than 100,000.
Under a provision to aid small businesses, the bill would exempt from clean-up cost liability all generators, arrangers and transporters of municipal solid waste and municipal sewage sludge.
